note: The closed vocabulary a reader can search on. These are CONSENSUS attributes: what most viewers would agree about a film, not measurements taken from it. They are deliberately NOT the recorded facets (genre, country, era, director, movement live in discovery.json) and NOT the five behavioural axes (dread/cruelty/irony/ambiguity/fracture, scored from plot text in fingerprints). This layer answers 'what is it like to watch, and what is it about', which is the thing a person types.
designNote: Re-derived from our own corpus and from what people actually ask for. The 1996 Ultimate Movie Thesaurus was read as a report on what a professional human editor thought worth categorising (docs/specs/thesaurus-evaluation.md) — its finding that ~0.3% of a 1,698-category vocabulary is about photography or tempo, and that 96 categories go to PLOT SHAPE, shaped the balance below: seven story shapes, and a texture group kept small and confined to things a viewer notices without a stopwatch. No category name, no assignment and no similar-films pair was copied from it.

groups.pace: How the film moves in time.
groups.tone: The attitude the film takes toward its own material.
groups.mood: The atmosphere the viewer sits inside.
groups.subject: What the film is about.
groups.story: The shape the story makes, independent of what it is about.
groups.texture: The surface a viewer notices without needing a stopwatch.
groups.mode: The kind of experience being offered.

attributes.gloss: Propulsive and unrelenting; it does not let you sit down. Whiplash, Mad Max: Fury Road.
attributes.not: Not merely 'has action scenes'. A slow film with one chase is not relentless.

attributes.gloss: Light on its feet — moves quickly and cleanly without adrenaline. Screwball, caper, farce.
attributes.not: Not relentless. Brisk is quick; relentless is pressure.

attributes.gloss: Deliberate accumulation: pressure builds over a long stretch before it breaks.
attributes.not: Not just 'slow'. Something must be tightening.

attributes.gloss: Time is given rather than spent; stillness, duration, room to look. Ozu, Tarkovsky, Tsai.
attributes.not: Not boring, and not slow-burn — nothing is being wound up.

attributes.gloss: The film believes something can be repaired, and leaves the viewer holding that.
attributes.not: Not 'happy ending'. A bleak film can end well; a hopeful film can end badly.

attributes.gloss: Offers no consolation and does not pretend to. The world is as it is.
attributes.not: Not merely sad or violent. Bleakness is the refusal of comfort.

attributes.gloss: Suffused with a soft, liveable sadness; loss that is felt rather than fought.
attributes.not: Not bleak. Melancholy is tender about its losses.

attributes.gloss: Meant to be funny, and is. Laughter is one of the things it is for.
attributes.not: Not the same as absurd, which is about the logic rather than the intent.

attributes.gloss: Says one thing and means another; keeps a knowing distance from its own surface.
attributes.not: Not sarcasm, and not comedy. A tragedy can be ironic.

attributes.gloss: Sincere and unguarded; means exactly what it shows, with no protective distance.
attributes.not: Not naive or simple. Earnestness is a stance, not a limitation.

attributes.gloss: Wants to be thought about; puts ideas ahead of feeling and expects work from you.
attributes.not: Not 'difficult'. A clear film can be cerebral, a confusing one need not be.

attributes.gloss: Treats its people gently and is interested in their care for each other.
attributes.not: Not romance as a genre. A war film can be tender.

attributes.gloss: Obeys the rules of a dream: images and associations before cause and effect.
attributes.not: Not merely surreal imagery. The film's logic must be the dream's.

attributes.gloss: Something bad is coming and the air knows it. Dread as an atmosphere.
attributes.not: Not gore, and not jump scares. Menace is the wait.

attributes.gloss: Somebody is watching, listening, or lying, and the film withholds who.
attributes.not: Not general suspense. Paranoia needs an unseen agency.

attributes.gloss: Companionable and lit from inside; a film you sit inside rather than endure.
attributes.not: Not sentimental, and not simply happy.

attributes.gloss: Cold, severe, stripped of ornament — in image, sound and behaviour alike.
attributes.not: Not low budget. Austerity is chosen.

attributes.gloss: Mourns a world that has already gone: a trade, a generation, a way of living.
attributes.not: Not simply set in the past.

attributes.gloss: Interested in bodies, surfaces, appetite, heat; the image wants to be touched.
attributes.not: Not explicitness. A chaste film can be sensual.

attributes.gloss: The world runs on a broken logic that nobody in it questions.
attributes.not: Not comedy, though it often is funny.

attributes.gloss: Faith, grace, the sacred, or the search for meaning beyond the material.
attributes.not: Not merely containing a church or a priest.

attributes.gloss: Power, the state, ideology, or who gets to decide — as the actual subject.
attributes.not: Not any film with a historical setting.

attributes.gloss: The passage out of childhood, filmed while it happens.
attributes.not: Not any film with a young protagonist.

attributes.gloss: Bereavement and what a person does with it.
attributes.not: Not any film containing a death.

attributes.gloss: A person consumed by a pursuit past the point of reason.
attributes.not: Not simple determination or professional focus.

attributes.gloss: Parents, children, siblings, inheritance — the family as the film's real arena.
attributes.not: Not any film with a family in it.

attributes.gloss: Wanting a person: love, lust, longing, and what wanting costs.
attributes.not: Not romance as a plot mechanism.

attributes.gloss: Labour and craft: the job done properly, the trade, the crew, the process.
attributes.not: Not any film with a professional protagonist.

attributes.gloss: Remembering as the film's business: the past worked over, doubted or reconstructed.
attributes.not: Not merely containing flashbacks.

attributes.gloss: Money and social station, and the walls between people made of them.
attributes.not: Not any film about poverty.

attributes.gloss: A return to a place or a people left behind, and what the return costs.
attributes.not: Not any journey.

attributes.gloss: Someone lands where they do not belong and the film is about the mismatch.
attributes.not: Not simple travel.

attributes.gloss: A clock is running and the film is organised around beating it.
attributes.not: Not general urgency.

attributes.gloss: A person comes apart over the course of the film, and it is the arc.
attributes.not: Not a single bad night.

attributes.gloss: Someone is trying to find out what happened, and finding out is the plot.
attributes.not: Not any crime film.

attributes.gloss: A wrong was done and the film is the answering of it.
attributes.not: Not any violent conflict.

attributes.gloss: Staying alive is the whole problem: the elements, the siege, the walk out.
attributes.not: Not general danger.

attributes.gloss: People barely speak; the film carries itself on image, action and silence.
attributes.not: Not a silent film by era — that is a record fact.

attributes.gloss: Dialogue-driven: the talking is the event, and there is a great deal of it.
attributes.not: Not merely having a script.

attributes.gloss: The composed image is one of the reasons the film exists; it is made to be looked at.
attributes.not: Not 'has nice cinematography'. This must be a defining quality.

attributes.gloss: Rough, immediate, documentary-adjacent; the camera is in the room and not hidden.
attributes.not: Not low budget by itself.

attributes.gloss: Heightened and designed — colour, décor, performance or blocking pushed past the real.
attributes.not: Not 'period costume'.

attributes.gloss: Violence is shown rather than implied, and shown enough that people mention it.
attributes.not: Not any film with a fight or a war.

attributes.gloss: Music or song carries the film; the score or the numbers are how it moves.
attributes.not: Not any film with a memorable theme.

attributes.gloss: Dirt, sweat, damp, decay; a surface you can smell.
attributes.not: Not merely dark.

attributes.gloss: Time is shuffled, doubled or reversed, and the shuffling is the design.
attributes.not: Not a single framing flashback.

attributes.gloss: Many characters or several stories carried in parallel with no single lead.
attributes.not: Not a film with a large supporting cast.

attributes.gloss: Confined to one place, and the confinement is the point.
attributes.not: Not merely 'mostly indoors'.

attributes.gloss: Built as a chain of discrete episodes rather than one accumulating plot.
attributes.not: Not merely long.

attributes.gloss: The film turns on a revelation that reframes what came before.
attributes.not: Not any surprise.

attributes.gloss: A voice tells it: voice-over, a diary, a testimony, an address to camera.
attributes.not: Not an opening title card.

attributes.gloss: Off Earth: ships, stations, other worlds.
attributes.not: Not any science fiction.

attributes.gloss: A small town or village where everyone is known — the milieu, not the map.
attributes.not: Not simply rural.

attributes.gloss: The night city as a world: streets, neon, bars, the hours after everyone left.
attributes.not: Not any urban film.

attributes.gloss: Landscape that does not care: mountain, jungle, desert, ice, open sea.
attributes.not: Not any exterior.

attributes.gloss: Set ahead of its own making, and the future is part of the subject.
attributes.not: Not any speculative premise.

attributes.gloss: Physical action is a main pleasure on offer: chases, fights, movement.
attributes.not: Not any film containing violence.

attributes.gloss: Organised to make you anxious about what happens next, and good at it.
attributes.not: Not menace, which is atmosphere rather than mechanism.

attributes.gloss: Scale as an attraction: the sight of it is one of the reasons to go.
attributes.not: Not budget.
